[Section] Experimental setup ::: The Rotowire dataset
[source_id=51] To evaluate the effectiveness of our model, and demonstrate its flexibility at handling heavy data-structure made of several types of entities, we used the RotoWire dataset BIBREF10. It includes basketball games statistical tables paired with journalistic descriptions of the games, as can be seen in the example of Figure FIGREF1. The descriptions are professionally written and average 337 words with a vocabulary size of $11.3$K. There are 39 different record keys, and the average number of records (resp. entities) in a single data-structure is 628 (resp. 28). Entities are of two types, either team or player, and player descriptions depend on their involvement in the game. We followed the data partitions introduced with the dataset and used a train/validation/test sets of respectively $3,398$/727/728 (data-structure, description) pairs.
